messages:
jess (runtime): Heads-up — overnight we saw a 2.8x jump in median token latency for routes hitting eu-west when kernel-picker v2 rolled out. Not a full outage but SLA p99 is nudging the threshold.

ben (platform): Ack. Any idea whether this is kernel selection or batching-related?

jess (runtime): Early signs point to the new batching heuristic + different kernel choices for long-context shards. KV-cache hit ratio also dropped ~18% on those routes. Putting raw traces in the perf bucket now.

carlos (obs): I pulled the token-level waterfall for a sample trace — looks like token-generation stage time doubled while scheduling latency stayed flat. Added link to quick dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/services/perf/token-waterfall?trace=1801234567

emma (sre): We got paged for increased failover counts around the same time — is cross-region fallback kicking in more often? That would explain the eu-west spike + rollback traffic to us-east.

jess (runtime): Yep, routing decision logs show 3x increase in cross-region fallbacks for route /chat/stream: policy=cost_prefers_us then fallback on throttled dedicated pool. See snippet of routing log:

```
[2026-03-17T03:12:05Z] route=/chat/stream model=rw-xl kernel=v2 node=eu-west-2 decision=fallback->us-east-1 reason=capacity_throttle
[2026-03-17T03:12:06Z] kvcache: miss route=/chat/stream prefixKey=abc123
[2026-03-17T03:12:06Z] kernel-select: chose=v2 expected_latency=18ms measured_tail=42ms
```

ben (platform): Interesting the kernel-selected expected_latency was optimistic. Could be our kernel perf profile for long sequences is stale. When was the kernel profile last re-run?

jae (ml infra): We reprofiled kernels two weeks ago with synthetic seq=4096 samples — but production seq distribution shifted (more short+long mix). The kernel selector's cost model weights sequence variance poorly. I'll repro the selection with the real histogram export.

carlos (obs): Actionable asks:
- Add per-route token-level p50/p90/p99 tiles (token-gen vs kvcache vs kernel).
- Surface kvcache hit ratio by route and by prefix-window (30m).
- Plot cross-region fallback rate per route (1m, 15m) with annotation for deployments.

jess (runtime): +1 to all. Also propose a new sampled trace field: "kernel_choice_rationale" that records which cost model term tipped the decision (latency estimate vs flops vs kv-affinity). That will help us correlate selector mistakes with perf.

emma (sre): For immediate mitigation can we pin eu-west traffic to the older kernel for canary percent until we fix the cost model? I don't want a rollback across the fleet.

ben (platform): We can do a canary override: route-tag=eu-west force_kernel=v1 for 10% of traffic or by prefix. I'll spin up a canary config and add a short-lived policy.

devops-bot: deploy:kernel-override-eu-west started by ben at 2026-03-17T04:01:12Z — rollout 0% -> 10%

jess (runtime): Thanks. Meanwhile I'll add a lightweight tracing patch to include kernel_choice_rationale + per-token timestamps. Lightweight to avoid extra overhead: boolean flags and a single packed label.

carlos (obs): I can add dashboard tiles today. Suggest thresholds: token-gen p99 > 120ms -> alert, kvcache hit ratio drop > 10% -> warn. Also add synthetic probe from eu-west to measure cross-region penalty independent of routing.

jae (ml infra): Reprofiling with production seq histogram now. Will post results and a diff of the cost model by EOD. If we see kernels actually slower for tails on mixed sequences we'll adjust selector weights.

emma (sre): When do we expected to flip the canary back or escalate to rollback? If p99 stays > 200ms for 30m we should roll back fully.

jess (runtime): Agreed. Let's reassess at 04:40 UTC after the canary warms. If kernel-choice-rationale traces show incorrect estimator hits, we'll revert.

ben (platform): Canary config is live (10%). Routing logs show the override in effect. I'll keep the rollout paused.

carlos (obs): Added dashboard: "Per-route token breakdown (eu-west)" and an annotation stream for deploys. Short link: https://dashboards.redwood/s/dash/dxhK2 (pinned to eng-runtime)

jess (runtime): Quick note on KV cache behavior — the drop aligns with a small change in prefix eviction policy we shipped last week. The new policy reduces memory bloat but seems to evict hot prefixes for certain long-chat flows. I'll run a sim comparing lru vs windowed-lru on the observed traces.

jae (ml infra): If kvcache misses drive kernel-selection to pick different kernels (because affinity cost term changes), that creates a feedback loop. We should instrument that path explicitly.

emma (sre): Good catch. Add a correlation alert: route-level kvcache_hit_ratio drop correlated with cross-region fallback > 2x -> pager.

ben (platform): I'll own the canary rollback plan and the kernel pin. jess + jae + carlos please own selector telemetry + dashboard tiles. Emma will own alert thresholds & runbook updates.

jess (runtime): Thanks all — I'll post trace samples and a short write-up of kernel-selection repro steps in #eng-runtime once I have them.

carlos (obs): Will follow up with dashboard links + alert rules in the ticket. Ticket created: INF-4823.

devops-bot: incident-note: INF-4823 created by carlos at 2026-03-17T04:05:01Z

ben (platform): Next sync in 30m unless something noisy happens. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
